chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Hasaan from Sahl ibn Darih from his father from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who retains his saliva out of respect for Allah, the Exalted, in his prayer, Allah will grant him health until death.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of retaining saliva during prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, this narration links the physical act of restraint during prayer to a specific divine reward, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a means of attaining *tawfiq* (divine facilitation). The promise of health until death underscores the holistic nature of worship in Shia tradition, where spiritual reverence manifests in bodily well-being, a concept often discussed by scholars like Al-Kulayni in the context of *amal al-salih* (righteous deeds).

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) from Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Ali b. Ahmad from Sahl b. Darihi from his father from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who retains his saliva during Salat out of respect of Allah’s Majesty and His Honor, Allah keeps him healthy till his death.”
